text:
ashley: seeing a burst of OOMs on prod after today's autobatching + fastpath kernel merge. node-pool-3. kv-cache steadily climbing, slab fragmentation visible in logs. putting rollout on hold.

raj: any CI perf failures or just prod?

olivia: CI was green for unit/integration but perf-run shows p99 regressions for longctx workloads (~18% worse). link: https://perf.internal/runs/1234

ben: bisect started. initial suspect commit is abc1234 (autobatch fastpath + prefetch tweaks). will try reverting the fastpath change in a canary.

ashley: thanks, flagged as rollout hold: infra/rollout-holds#432. canary only for now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started -> prod-canary-7 (image: rwinf/serving:stable+abc1234)

olivia: uploaded a profile (heap + alloc traces) to /artifacts/heap-2012345678.pb. quick grep shows big chunks in cache.pin_entries() and prefetch buffer retention. sequence-length distribution shifted right in canary traffic (more longctxs).

ben: local reproduce: run loadgen with seqlen=4096 -> kv arena grows until OOM. snippet:```
E 10:42:31 alloc failed: arena_size=2.1G, pinned=1.9G
kv_slot(0x7f...): owner=cache.pin_entries
```

raj: could autobatch prefetch be increasing KV lifetime? If prefetch holds kv refs until next token, that would balloon memory for longctx.

olivia: yes, autobatch fastpath added 'prefetch_next_kv' to reduce token latency. tradeoff: longer kv pin windows. that's likely sequence-length sensitive.

ben: temporary mitigation: flip kernel-selector to legacy for canary and lower kv-evict-threshold. commands: `kubectl set env deploy/serving KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy --namespace=prod-canary` and add flag `--kv-evict-threshold=0.65`

infra-bot: perf-ci report: jenkins/perf/456 -> throughput -7%, mem-alloc +24% on longctx, link: https://ci.internal/jenkins/job/perf/456

ashley: if legacy kernel + lower evict helps in canary, we should revert fastpath until we redesign prefetch semantics. please open revert PR to main and mark as rollback candidate.

ben: opened PR #782 revert(autobatch-fastpath): https://git.internal/rwinf/pulls/782. attaching perf traces and heap dump.

olivia: additional note: KV fragmentation increases GC pressure; consider coalescing free lists and lowering pin granularity as long-term fix.

raj: agree. for now hold the rollout and revert main if canary stabilizes. I'll coordinate with capacity planning for a temporary burst in mem usage.

ashley: thanks all. watching metrics; will update when canary stabilizes or if we need immediate revert to main. :thumbsup:
